name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *all* PRs for one week first. This gives us real-world data on its impact without risking disruption. The trade-off is delayed feedback loops, but we avoid breaking builds or annoying devs with false positives. After a week, we’ll have hard numbers to decide if we adopt it permanently.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode risks normalizing PR-Agent noise—reviewers will ignore *all* comments, including real ones, by week’s end. A better alternative: run it on a *single team’s PRs* for a week, then compare their review load and merge times to a control group. If merge times spike or reviewers still ignore 90% of comments, the tool fails the test.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent on *only* PRs that have no reviewers assigned yet—this cuts the shadow mode workload in half while still capturing the riskiest cases. If merge times or review quality don’t degrade in a week, expand to all PRs.

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent on PRs with no reviewers for a week. This targets the highest-risk cases—unreviewed PRs—without wasting effort on already-monitored ones. The trade-off is missing edge cases where reviewers are assigned late, but we’ll catch those in the next phase. If merge times and review quality stay stable, we’ll expand to all PRs next week.
